title: CES 2027 Las Vegas travel guide and tips
summary: Plan your CES 2027 trip to Las Vegas with hotel guidance, flight trends, transportation tips, per diem rates, and advice for navigating the show.
body_markdown:
Owned and produced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), CES 2027 will take place across the LVCC, Venetian, and C Space campuses.\[1\]\[2\] With exhibits, conference sessions, product demonstrations, meetings, and media events spread across Las Vegas, a little planning before you arrive means you can spend more of the week exploring relevant technologies, connecting with industry professionals, and bringing useful ideas back to your team.


## What is CES and who is it for?


CES is an annual trade show owned and produced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). The event brings established technology companies, startups, investors, industry professionals, policymakers, and media to venues across Las Vegas.\[1\]\[2\]


CES is a trade-only event for people affiliated with the consumer technology industry. It isn't open to the general public, and all attendees must be at least 18.\[4\] Attendees include product and engineering leaders, startup founders, investors, marketers, media professionals, retailers, manufacturers, and government representatives. They come to explore emerging technologies, evaluate products and potential partners, attend conference sessions, meet with industry peers, and follow developments across sectors ranging from artificial intelligence and mobility to digital health and entertainment.


Independently audited CES 2026 participation figures provide a useful look at the event's scale: 148,392 participants, more than 4,100 exhibitors, approximately 1,200 startups in Eureka Park, more than 400 conference sessions, and more than 1,400 speakers across more than 2.6 million net square feet of exhibit space.\[5\]\[6\]


Before you arrive, identify the technologies, companies, and conversations most relevant to your goals. A clear set of priorities can help you decide which campuses to visit, which sessions to attend, and where to leave room for product demonstrations and unplanned conversations.


## What makes CES 2027 worth the trip


CES gives attendees opportunities to see emerging technologies in person, watch live demonstrations, speak directly with the teams developing new products, and connect with potential partners from across the technology industry.\[1\]\[7\] Whether you're evaluating solutions, tracking developments in your industry, meeting startups and investors, or covering product announcements, the event brings together experiences and conversations that can be difficult to replicate remotely.


Plan your time around these in-person experiences:


- **LVCC show floor:** Explore exhibits across Central, West, North, and South halls, with technology spanning mobility, artificial intelligence, energy, smart communities, entertainment, product design, and sourcing.\[8\]
- **Eureka Park:** Meet early-stage companies exhibiting at Venetian Expo and discover new products while connecting with founders, investors, media, and potential partners.\[5\]\[9\]
- **C Space:** Attend programming and meetings for the advertising, marketing, media, entertainment, and content industries at ARIA and other C Space Campus venues.\[7\]
- **CES Foundry:** Explore dedicated AI and quantum technology programming, demonstrations, and networking at Fontainebleau.\[1\]\[7\]
- **Keynotes and conference sessions:** Hear technology and business leaders discuss emerging trends, industry challenges, and the developments shaping their organizations.
- **Media Days and CES Unveiled:** Registered media can attend advance product announcements, press conferences, CTA's technology trends presentation, and CES Unveiled before the exhibit floor opens.\[7\]


The value of CES isn't measured by how many sessions you attend or booths you visit. It's what you bring back: a clearer understanding of emerging technologies, potential solutions and partners, stronger industry relationships, and ideas your team can put into practice.


## Where to stay for CES 2027


Choosing the right hotel depends on which CES campus you'll visit most often. Staying near the Las Vegas Convention Center can simplify exhibit-floor days, while hotels near Venetian Expo or ARIA may be more convenient for Eureka Park, C Space programming, and nearby meetings.

If your schedule centers on the LVCC exhibit halls, choose a hotel with a manageable walking route, Monorail access, or a direct CES shuttle. If you'll spend significant time at Eureka Park or other Venetian Expo programming, consider staying at The Venetian or The Palazzo. For C Space programming and meetings, ARIA, Vdara, Cosmopolitan, and Park MGM make up the official campus. Before booking, check the complete route to the venue and entrance you'll use most rather than assuming every Strip hotel is within convenient walking distance.


For additional hotel options, walk times, and loyalty-friendly choices, see our guide to[hotels near the Las Vegas Convention Center](https://navan.com/hotel-choices/las-vegas-convention-center) .


### Hotel pricing at CES 2027


Navan analyzed anonymized hotel booking patterns near the Las Vegas Convention Center during CES week 2026 to provide context for hotel pricing.\[14\] Use these benchmarks while planning your trip:


- **Median hotel rate:** The median nightly rate during CES week was $439, approximately 63% higher than the $269 median during a quieter week later that January.\[14\]
- **Stay length:** Business travelers booked an average stay of 2.8 nights.\[14\]
- **Late bookings:** Approximately 32% of CES-week stays were booked within two weeks of arrival.\[14\]
- **Booking window:** Travelers who booked one to two months ahead paid a median nightly rate of $407, compared with $594 for those booking two to four weeks ahead. Bookings made during the final seven days had a median rate of $314.\[14\]


Official CES 2027 housing is open through onPeak, CTA's designated housing agent. The official housing program offers rooms at hotels throughout Las Vegas, but rates increase as January approaches and some properties sell out.\[12\]


If you're booking through the official CES hotel program, keep these points in mind:


- **Use the official booking site:** Access onPeak through ces.tech. CTA identifies onPeak as the only official housing agent for CES 2027 and warns attendees about unaffiliated companies claiming to offer official rooms.\[12\]
- **Choose the right reservation type:** Individual reservations are available for up to nine rooms. Request a group block if you need 10 or more rooms on a single night.\[12\]
- **Compare total cost:** Resort fees, parking, deposits, and cancellation policies vary by hotel, so look beyond the nightly room rate before booking.
- **Choose your location carefully:** Staying near the campus where you'll spend most of your time may be more valuable than simply booking the lowest available rate.


### Las Vegas flight trends


Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) is the primary airport for CES attendees.\[15\] Navan flight data from the January 2026 event week includes 2,510 business travel bookings to Las Vegas, with 17.4% originating outside the U.S.\[14\] The most common origin locations were New York, Newark, San Francisco, San Jose, and Los Angeles.


Arriving on Tuesday, Jan. 5, provides general attendees time to check into your hotel and collect your badge before the exhibit floor opens Wednesday. Registered media and attendees participating in Tuesday conference programming may need to arrive earlier. CES requires attendees to collect their own badges at a remote pickup location before entering a show venue.\[4\]\[7\]

## How to budget for CES 2027 in Las Vegas


Plan your CES 2027 budget around the full cost of the trip, including registration, lodging, transportation, meals, and other travel expenses. Account for these costs upfront, and you can set a realistic budget before requesting approval.


### Federal per diem for Las Vegas


The U.S. General Services Administration sets federal per diem rates for lodging, meals, and incidental expenses. These rates apply to federal employees traveling on official business, although some companies also use them as benchmarks when setting travel budgets and reimbursement limits.


For CES 2027, the FY2027 rates for Las Vegas and Clark County are:


- **$259 per day combined:** Includes $173 for nightly lodging plus $86 for daily meals and incidental expenses (M&IE)\[13\]
- **M&IE breakdown:** Includes $22 for breakfast, $23 for lunch, $36 for dinner, and $5 for incidentals (reduce your meal allowance for any meals provided at the event when required)\[13\]
- **First and last travel days:** Includes an M&IE allowance of $64.50, or 75% of the daily M&IE rate\[13\]


The $173 federal lodging allowance is considerably lower than the $439 median nightly rate in Navan's CES-week 2026 hotel data.\[13\]\[14\] If your company uses GSA rates as a benchmark, compare hotels outside the immediate LVCC area and account for transportation costs before choosing a lower nightly rate.


### Other expenses to consider


Planning for these expenses before you book can make it easier to stay within budget and avoid surprises when it's time to submit your expense report.


- **Conference registration:** The Standard Pass costs $149 through Nov. 30, 2026, and increases to $349 beginning Dec. 1. The Premium Pass costs $1,450 through Nov. 30 and $1,750 starting Dec. 1.\[4\]
- **Registration add-ons:** Show-floor tours, discounted Las Vegas Monorail tickets, the CES 2027 Trends Report, and select conference tracks and programs are available for an additional cost.\[4\]
- **Airport transportation:** Budget for a taxi, rideshare, or public transit between LAS and your hotel. RTC Route 108 connects Terminal 1 with Paradise Road and the LVCC area; travelers arriving at Terminal 3 must take the interterminal shuttle to the Terminal 1 bus stop.\[15\]\[16\]
- **Meals:** Budget for meals that aren't included with a conference session or event. If catering is provided, check whether your company requires you to reduce your daily meal allowance.
- **Client dinners:** Upscale restaurants and private dining near the CES campuses can cost $75-$175 per person before drinks.
- **Transportation between venues:** CES provides complimentary transportation on select routes, but you may still need to budget for rideshares or taxis when shuttles don't align with your schedule.\[8\]
- **After-hours networking:** Leave room in your budget for partner receptions, team dinners, and other informal networking events.


## Plan your CES agenda


CES spans 12 venues and more than 2.5 million net square feet, making it impossible to cover every exhibit, session, and event. Start by identifying the technologies, companies, and sessions most relevant to your goals, then leave time for the exhibit halls, product demonstrations, meetings, and travel between campuses.\[2\]\[7\]


Here's a high-level look at the week:\[7\]


- **Monday (Jan. 4):** Media Day 1 and CES Unveiled at Mandalay Bay for registered media
- **Tuesday (Jan. 5):** Media Day 2, conference sessions, and C Space programming; exhibit halls remain closed
- **Wednesday (Jan. 6):** Exhibit halls open, with conference programming, C Space, CES Foundry, and show-floor press conferences
- **Thursday (Jan. 7):** Full day of exhibits, conference sessions, C Space programming, CES Foundry, and press conferences
- **Friday (Jan. 8):** Exhibits, conference sessions, C Space programming, and CES Foundry continue
- **Saturday (Jan. 9):** Final day of exhibits; conference programming, C Space, and CES Foundry are closed


The complete session catalog and 2027 CES App will continue to take shape as the event approaches. Once available, use the app to build your agenda, save exhibitors, navigate the show floor, and review transportation information.\[10\]


### Build a plan around your priorities


Review the session and exhibitor catalogs before the event, and build your schedule around the sessions, companies, and technologies most relevant to your work. Group activities by campus whenever possible, then leave room for demonstrations, unscheduled conversations, and the time required to move between venues.


Here are a few ways to prepare before you arrive:


- **Sessions:** Save your must-attend keynotes and conference sessions in the CES App or online planner, then leave substantial blocks for the exhibit halls.
- **Meetings:** Contact exhibitors, partners, customers, or colleagues about two weeks before CES to schedule booth meetings or coffee chats.
- **Logistics:** Confirm remote badge pickup hours, download the CES App when the 2027 version becomes available, and save the locations of the LVCC, Venetian Expo, and any C Space venues on your agenda.\[4\]\[8\]\[10\]
- **Contacts:** Decide whether you'll exchange contact information through LinkedIn, digital business cards, or Attendee Connect — if it returns in the 2027 CES App — and add a brief note after each conversation to preserve context.


Once you know which days and campuses your agenda will cover, use our[business trip planning guide](https://navan.com/blog/edge/how-to-plan-a-business-trip) to coordinate your flights, hotel, and departure plans around your schedule.


## What to pack and wear at CES


Most CES attendees dress in business casual or tech casual attire, such as jeans or chinos, collared shirts, sweaters, and comfortable sneakers. If you're meeting with customers, investors, executives, or potential partners outside the conference, consider packing a blazer or another business-casual option for dinners and evening events.


January in Las Vegas typically brings daytime highs around 58°F (14°C) and overnight lows near 39°F (4°C), with limited rainfall and low humidity.\[18\] You'll move between indoor exhibit halls and outdoor routes connecting hotels and venues, so pack layers that are easy to add or remove.


### Conference essentials


A few practical items can make long days of exhibits, sessions, demonstrations, and meetings more comfortable. Add these essentials to your packing list:


- **Two pairs of comfortable shoes:** You'll cover considerable ground across the LVCC halls and other CES campuses.
- **Portable charger:** The CES App, maps, messaging, note-taking, and photos can quickly drain your phone's battery.
- **Reusable water bottle:** Las Vegas's dry climate makes it important to drink water throughout the day.
- **Lip balm and moisturizer:** Low humidity and long days indoors can leave your skin and lips feeling dry.
- **Throat lozenges and hand sanitizer:** Crowded halls and hours of conversation can take a toll.
- **Light sweater or jacket:** Exhibit halls and meeting rooms may feel cooler than the temperature outside.
- **Small backpack or laptop bag:** Carry your charger, water bottle, meeting materials, and other essentials comfortably throughout the day.


## Getting from the airport to CES venues


Harry Reid International Airport (LAS) is approximately 4 miles south of the Las Vegas Convention Center and provides convenient access to hotels across the Strip.\[11\]\[15\] General attendees may want to arrive Tuesday, Jan. 5, so they have time to check in and collect their CES badge before the exhibit floor opens Wednesday. Registered media and attendees participating in Tuesday programming may need to arrive earlier.


For most attendees traveling with luggage, a rideshare or taxi is the simplest option. RTC Route 108 offers a lower-cost alternative for travelers staying near Paradise Road or the LVCC, while third-party airport shuttles may work for hotels along their routes.

CES requires attendees to collect their own badges at a remote pickup location before entering an exhibit venue. Badge pickup is available at LAS and select hotels, but locations and hours vary by date.\[4\]\[7\]


Once you're at your hotel, use the Las Vegas Monorail, Vegas Loop, CES shuttles, or rideshare based on the campus you're visiting. The Monorail serves the LVCC but doesn't stop at Venetian Expo. CES operates the Tech Express between the LVCC and Venetian Expo, while complimentary hotel shuttles connect select official CES hotels with the LVCC and Venetian Expo.\[8\]


## Beyond sessions: Make time for exhibit halls and networking


Some of the most valuable parts of CES happen outside scheduled sessions. Leave time in your agenda for the LVCC show floor, Eureka Park, product demonstrations, exhibitor meetings, and conversations between events rather than filling every hour with conference programming.


- **Schedule meetings before you arrive:** Contact exhibitors, partners, customers, and colleagues about two weeks before CES to arrange booth meetings or coffee chats.
- **Plan around your priority exhibitors:** Review the exhibitor directory and identify the companies and technologies most relevant to your work before building your route.
- **Group visits by campus:** Visit exhibitors in the same hall or campus together to reduce unnecessary travel between the LVCC, Venetian Expo, and C Space.
- **Leave dedicated time for Eureka Park:** If startups and emerging technologies are a priority, reserve a substantial block for exploring Eureka Park at Venetian Expo.\[9\]
- **Use the CES App:** Save exhibitors, map your route, review schedule changes, and check transportation information while you're at the event.\[10\]
- **Take notes after each conversation:** Record important product details, questions, and next steps while the discussion is still fresh.
- **Follow up within 48 hours:** Send a brief email or LinkedIn message that references the conversation and identifies a clear next step.
- **Build in short breaks:** Four days of exhibits, sessions, meetings, and travel between campuses can be tiring. Leave time to eat, drink water, and recharge throughout the day.


The best networking begins before CES and continues after you leave. A smaller number of relevant conversations with clear follow-up actions will generally be more useful than visiting as many booths as possible or collecting contacts without context.


## What to eat at CES 2027


Long days of exhibits, demonstrations, sessions, and meetings can make it easy to skip meals or rely on snacks. Start the day with a filling breakfast, keep a protein bar or another easy snack in your bag, and stay hydrated so you're not running on coffee alone by midafternoon.


When it's time for a client dinner, team meal, or quick lunch, these options are convenient to the LVCC Campus:


- **Client dinner:** Piero's Italian Cuisine at 355 Convention Center Drive offers Italian and seafood dishes, along with private dining for groups. Smart or business casual attire is required.\[17\]
- **Late team meal:** The Peppermill Restaurant on Las Vegas Boulevard serves diner-style American food late into the night. It's open 24 hours Thursday-Sunday and from 7 a.m.-2 a.m. Monday-Wednesday.\[22\]
- **Quick lunch:** Restaurants and concession stands throughout the LVCC provide convenient options when you don't have enough time to leave the campus between sessions or meetings.\[11\]


If you're planning a client dinner or team meal, reserve it before you arrive. Navan Edge can book Las Vegas restaurants in the same chat where you arrange your flight and hotel.


## Finish strong on departure day


Before you check out, take a few minutes to organize your receipts, notes, and new contacts so you're not sorting through the week after you return home. Travelers departing after the final exhibit day should also allow extra time at LAS as CES attendees begin leaving Las Vegas.


- **Pack the night before:** Charge your devices, lay out your travel clothes, and check the room for chargers, badges, and anything else you may have left behind.
- **Confirm late checkout:** If you have an evening flight, ask the front desk about late checkout or have Navan Edge coordinate the request on your behalf.
- **Arrive early at the airport:** LAS can be especially busy after a large convention, so allow at least two hours for domestic flights and three hours for international departures.
- **Submit expenses early:** Upload receipts while the trip's meals, transportation, and hotel charges are still easy to remember, and note any lodging above your company's allowance when you file.
- **Visit the airport lounge:** If you have lounge access, use the time to organize notes, respond to messages, or begin following up before boarding.
- **Schedule a debrief:** Block time early the following week to share useful findings, reconnect with new contacts, and turn ideas from CES into clear next steps for your team.


## Make the most of your CES 2027 trip


CES 2027 brings technology companies, startups, investors, media, and industry professionals together across Las Vegas. Choose your hotel based on the campus where you'll spend most of your time, build a realistic travel budget, prioritize the exhibits and sessions most relevant to your goals, and leave room for demonstrations and conversations between scheduled events.


A little planning before you arrive can help you return home with a clearer understanding of emerging technologies, useful industry connections, and ideas your team can put into practice.
